criteria.text: X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH), the closed FDA-labeled indication in this PDF.
Patient is 1 year of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a nephrologist or endocrinologist (approval criterion 2).
XLH confirmed by genetic testing (e.g. PHEX mutation) AND baseline serum FGF23 level obtained (approval criterion 3).
Baseline fasting serum phosphorus documented below the normal range for age (approval criterion 4).
At least 2 months of calcitriol plus oral phosphate, or contraindication/intolerance, with phosphate levels documented before and after supplementation (approval criterion 5).
Any oral phosphate and vitamin D analog discontinued for at least one week prior to therapy (approval criterion 6).
Prescriber agrees to monitor and document serum phosphorus throughout therapy (approval criterion 7).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Crysvita (burosumab-twza), an FGF23 blocking antibody, Criteria Version 1: Original 03/7/2019 (printed 03/7//2019); Approval 04/19/2019; Effective 06/10/2019.

Encoded: closed XLH indication and approval criteria 1-7. Denial criteria mirror the approval requirements. Genetic confirmation and baseline FGF23 are both required; no numeric FGF23 threshold is stated. Baseline phosphorus and therapy history are documentation attestations.

Cautions: do not use with oral phosphate and active vitamin D analogs. Pretherapy washout is encoded; ongoing combination avoidance remains notes only. Do not initiate if serum phosphorus is within or above normal for age (covered by baseline phosphorus criterion).
Cautions (notes only): contraindicated in severe renal impairment or end stage renal disease (ESRD). This is not a separate denial predicate.

Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months with documented improvement in phosphorus levels AND positive clinical response, e.g. decreased bone pain or improvement in skeletal deformities.
Quantity limits (notes only): 10 mg/ml vial: 2 per 28 days; 20 mg/ml vial: 2 per 28 days; 30 mg/ml vial: 6 per 28 days. Numeric quantity enforcement is not encoded.
Documentation verification, remaining cautions, duration, reauthorization response and quantity limits require manual review; this pack remains partial. No alternatives are specified.
